title: Indra with the Maruts, drink the soma here

sandhi_exceptions.note: शार्याते अपिबः: the locative’s -e stays before a, unjoined, as the Saṃhitā writes it.

words.context: Bhāskara explains the -s ending of the vocative («मतुवसोः»)
Sāyaṇa: at the rite of king Śaryāti’s son

words.meaning: in the shelter, in the protection
they seek to win, they serve

sandhi.rule: a final n after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel (P. 8.3.32 (ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्))

morphology.note: instrumental singular with the old long -ī for -yā; Bhāskara cites the sūtra सुपां सुलुक् for it.
locative singular without the ending -i, a Vedic form.

translation.literal: Indra, with the Maruts, drink the soma here, as you drank of the pressed at Śaryāta’s; under your guidance, in your shelter, hero, the poets who sacrifice well seek to win [you].
translation.readable: Indra, with your Maruts, drink the soma here, as you drank the pressed soma at the sacrifice of Śaryāti’s son. Under your guidance and in your shelter, hero, the wise who sacrifice well come to serve you.

meaning: An invitation to Indra, with his troop of storm-gods the Maruts, to drink the soma here as he once drank it at the sacrifice of Śaryāti’s son (RV 3.51.7; TS 1.4.18.1). The wise who sacrifice well seek him under his guidance and in his shelter. In the Saṃhitā it is the verse with which the second marutvatīya cup of soma is drawn, at the midday pressing. The verse addresses Indra.
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Bṛhaspati’s step in the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, so the edition does not say which this verse is for; the verse itself addresses Indra. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara gives its use in the Saṃhitā: «द्वितीयं मरुत्वतीयं गृह्णाति» — the second cup for Indra with the Maruts is drawn with this four-pāda triṣṭubh.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara names the king: «शर्यातिर् नाम राजा», and the soma Indra drank was at Śaryāti’s rite.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda, says the story is told in the Kauṣītaki: «इन्द्रः शार्यातस्य यज्ञे सोमरसानपिबदित्येषोऽर्थः कौषीतके स्पष्टमुक्तः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh. The hiatus शार्याते अपिबः is kept as the Saṃhitā writes it (declared above); in मरुत्व इह the visarga has fallen before a vowel, the regular treatment.
